Young owl-wolf body, mottled fur, downy dark wing-feathers along the back, upright ears, and cautious forward posture.

Pure startled instinct in a body it has not grown into yet. Bright frightened eyes, ears that swivel at every snapped twig, paws a size too big. It wants its mother and cannot understand why the road brought strangers instead.

Foxlike face, oversized bat ears, delicate folded wings, tiny paws on a mossy branch, and a mischievous expression warmed by Sablewood light.

Behavior

A pocket of curiosity with folded-cloak wings, perched where it can watch every hand at the card table. Bonded to Halython without being owned by anyone. Reads a room faster than most people and judges it kindly.

Warning Signs

Being grabbed, caged, or treated as a party trick instead of a companion.

You Could -

  • Give it distance before deciding it is hostile.
  • Read posture, tracks, and what it is protecting.

Young Dryads - Player Handout

Field Guide PagePlayer-safe

Young Dryads

Creature / Animal

Player-safe note: Small sapling spirits with bark-textured limbs, leaf hair, green-gold eyes, and shy defensive postures rooted around stones like children guarding a boundary.

Observed Form

Childlike sapling spirits with bark limbs, leaf hair, glowing green-gold eyes, shy defensive posture, roots around stones, spring leaves, and moss.

Behavior

Children of the wood with bark for skin, shy until a kindness is broken. They guard the stones like a held breath, and they only turn fierce when a guest takes the welcome they were given and spits on it.

Warning Signs

Axes and fire, the Hunting Trees that were once kin gone wrong, and guests who smile and then steal.

  • Give it distance before deciding it is hostile.

Heroic fire-safety crews who clear dangerous brush, sell fire wards, and are always, impressively, first on the scene.

Slogan

Fire Solutions™: ahead of the flames.

How To Deal

Fire Solutions™ rolls in like a parade of competence: orange water-wagons, crews in flame-bright livery, free Ember Alarms™ pressed into every hand. The crews are genuinely brave. It is just a remarkable coincidence how reliably the forest catches, and how...

You Could -

  • Ask what they publicly promise.
  • Compare their slogan to what they actually do in the scene.

Action Roll - Player Handout

Player Reference CardRules

Action Roll

core-roll

Roll when a PC does something uncertain and consequences matter.

What It Is

Roll when a PC does something uncertain and consequences matter.

How It Works

When a PC tries something uncertain and meaningful, choose a trait, set Difficulty, roll Hope d12 + Fear d12, add bonuses, compare total, then read Hope/Fear spin.

Try It

Give a player Presence 12 to calm a worried animal, then ask what Hope or Fear changes in the scene.

You Could -

  • Player states the action in the fiction.
  • GM names the trait that best matches the method and the Difficulty.
  • Player rolls Hope d12 + Fear d12 and adds trait, Experience, or advantage/disadvantage.
  • Compare total to Difficulty, then resolve the Hope/Fear or critical result.
